hypotheses: H1 (threshold sensitivity): for every index, candidate-change area decreases monotonically as the absolute threshold tightens from 0.05 to 0.25, and the ranking of the three indices by candidate-change fraction at the primary threshold is preserved across the sweep. Measured by the threshold-response sweep with area-conservation checks.

H2 (composite versus single scene): the 3x3-observation median composite yields a smaller absolute mean delta and a narrower single-pair spread than the nine genuine single-scene pairs, because per-scene observation noise (sun angle, tide, atmosphere) partially averages out. Measured by comparing the composite_median estimator against the single_pairs family.

H3 (temporal robustness): removing any single observation from a composite (leave-one-out) shifts the candidate-change fraction less than the full spread across single-scene pairs. Measured by the leave_one_out family against the single_pairs family at each threshold.

H4 (cross-pipeline consistency): the frozen M0 single-scene NDVI delta and the M1 anchor single-scene NDVI delta agree closely on their shared valid footprint because they use the same two dates and the same formula; residual differences are attributable to mask policy, not processing. Measured by the cross-pipeline comparison on shared pixels.

H5 (validity role): the common-valid footprint is complete for this study, so estimator differences are caused by observation selection, not by validity masks. Measured by the coverage summary and the per-estimator common-valid fractions.

uncertainty.interpretation: All intervals and ranges here describe resampling and observation-selection variability for this AOI and grid. None of them is a confidence interval about mangrove extent in general, and none validates a specific threshold as 'true' change.

interpretation_guardrails: Candidate-change areas are threshold-dependent descriptions of index difference, not verified environmental change.
For Coringa, an NDVI decrease is not evidence of mangrove loss: tides, seasonality and mixed pixels can produce the same signal.
No independent reference labels were used in this run; no supervised accuracy number is reported anywhere in it.
Estimator differences measure observation-selection effects, not processing errors.
